title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 1

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the introduction take place?
tasks.audioText: The machine tools department will introduce the main parts of a training lathe on Wednesday at nine. Students should meet in the theory classroom first, where the instructor will show a labelled diagram. The group will then observe the machine from the designated viewing area. No machine operation is planned during this introductory session.

tasks.prompt: A conventional lathe rotates a workpiece while a cutting tool removes material. The main components include the bed, headstock, tailstock and carriage. Each part has a different function, and the machine type determines the available operations. Before discussing a machine, students should use the correct component names and refer to the manufacturer's documentation for model-specific details. Reading 1. What rotates during a conventional turning operation?
Where should students look for model-specific information?
The workpiece ___ by the spindle during a turning operation.
Choose TWO parts commonly found on a conventional lathe.
The part of a lathe that supports and carries the cutting tool is the ___.
You are unsure which component is shown on a diagram. What should you ask?
options: I will call it any name.
Could you identify this component on the labelled diagram, please?
The component names are not important.
I will guess from its colour.

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words describing the main parts of a conventional lathe and explaining the function of two components.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
